cotton_bacterial_blight.immediate_steps: Remove infected leaves carefully, do not compost them, and clean tools after handling the plant.
cotton_bacterial_blight.treatment: A copper-based bactericide (copper oxychloride) labelled for cotton bacterial blight may help as a protectant — it does not cure plants once infected. Seed dressing with copper oxychloride also helps. Always follow the product label and local agricultural advice.
cotton_bacterial_blight.prevention: Rotate crops, use clean seed/plants, space plants for airflow, and avoid working with wet plants.
cotton_bacterial_blight.note: General guidance only. For chemical use, always follow the product label and local agricultural extension advice.
cotton_bacterial_blight.source: Plantix — Bacterial Blight of Cotton; UAF Faisalabad / AARI Dera Ghazi Khan field trials, Pakistan

cotton_curl_virus.immediate_steps: Pull out and destroy infected plants, and control whiteflies so the virus does not spread.
cotton_curl_virus.note: General guidance only. For chemical use, always follow the product label and local agricultural extension advice.
cotton_curl_virus.prevention: Use resistant or tolerant varieties, clean seed, and control whiteflies early in the season.
cotton_curl_virus.treatment: There is no cure for the virus itself. An insecticide labelled for whitefly, such as imidacloprid or acetamiprid, controls the insect that spreads it — always follow the product label and local agricultural advice. Rotate insecticide classes: whitefly in Punjab has developed resistance to neonicotinoids, so diafenthiuron or buprofezin are rotation options.
cotton_curl_virus.source: CABI Plantwise Plus Knowledge Bank — Pakistan factsheet: Cotton leaf curl virus (20147801354)

cotton_fusarium_wilt.immediate_steps: Pull out and destroy infected plants, and do not move soil from infested fields.
cotton_fusarium_wilt.note: General guidance only. For chemical use, always follow the product label and local agricultural extension advice.
cotton_fusarium_wilt.prevention: Use resistant or tolerant varieties, rotate crops, and use clean certified seed.
cotton_fusarium_wilt.treatment: There is no cure once plants are infected. Resistant varieties are the main defence. Carbendazim or thiophanate-methyl as a seed treatment before sowing may help, and a Trichoderma seed treatment may also reduce severity — always follow the product label and local agricultural advice.
cotton_fusarium_wilt.source: PARC — Handbook on Agriculture Pesticides 2018 (Carbendazim registered in Pakistan); Arysta/UPL Pakistan — Topsin-M 70 WP product label

healthy_cotton.immediate_steps: Monitor the plant regularly and keep leaves dry where possible.
healthy_cotton.treatment: No treatment needed. Keep balanced watering and feeding, and remove any dead leaves promptly.
healthy_cotton.prevention: Give good air circulation, avoid overwatering, and check leaves weekly so any new problem is caught early.
healthy_cotton.note: General guidance only. For chemical use, always follow the product label and local agricultural extension advice.

cotton_alternaria.immediate_steps: Remove and burn infected leaves and plant debris. Spray only if spots are spreading severely — light infections often do not reduce yield enough to justify a fungicide.
cotton_alternaria.note: General guidance only. For chemical use, always follow the product label and local agricultural extension advice.
cotton_alternaria.prevention: Use clean seed, remove and burn infected plant debris after harvest, rotate crops, avoid excess nitrogen, and correct potassium deficiency, which makes plants more susceptible.
cotton_alternaria.treatment: A protectant fungicide such as mancozeb or copper oxychloride, or a systemic triazole such as propiconazole, labelled for cotton Alternaria leaf spot, may help — always follow the product label and local agricultural advice.
cotton_alternaria.source: Plantix — Alternaria Leaf Spot of Cotton; Bhattiprolu et al. — field evaluation of fungicides against Alternaria leaf spot on cotton

cotton_verticillium_wilt.immediate_steps: Pull out and destroy infected plants, and do not move soil or plant debris from the infested field to clean fields.
cotton_verticillium_wilt.note: General guidance only. For chemical use, always follow the product label and local agricultural extension advice.
cotton_verticillium_wilt.prevention: Use resistant or tolerant varieties — the main defence — rotate with non-host crops such as cereals, use clean seed, and avoid excess nitrogen and excess irrigation.
cotton_verticillium_wilt.treatment: There is no cure once plants are infected, and no fungicide controls this disease. A Trichoderma seed treatment may reduce severity in the next crop — always follow the product label and local agricultural advice.
cotton_verticillium_wilt.source: Oklahoma State Extension — Verticillium wilt (no effective chemical control); Journal of Cotton Science (Hanson, 2000) — Trichoderma virens seed treatment
